questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always wanted to go to Australia so this was a peak opportunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the academic level isn't as high as at KU which has it's up and down sides.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: pretty easy. The worker from the university associated with exchange students helped out a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: don't remember any specifics. Only that the specific rooms and buildings were hard to locate

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at St Marks college. A tad pricier but definitely worth it. Had a fun college experience with loads of events and other social stuff. The other people at the several colleges Adelaide has are 18-22 years old so if you're older have that in mind.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: some of my other friends had shared housing in the suburbs around the city which they sounded happy with. Cheaper but a bit further from uni.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't really remember so there must not have been any problems

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: took screen shots of all my old courses' decriptions and had them translated via google translate. then put them all in a word document and sent it to the university so they could figure out what experience I had.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: an email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: yes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: just get the pre approval done quick and do it for multiple course so you can apply for courses when it opens and get it over with

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: not as thorough as in KU. Multiple assignments and quizzes with deadlines almost all the time. They accounted for some percentages of the final grade. Takes some pressure of the final exam with for my sake was 40-45%. But you had to keep up the whole time for quizzes and the midterm. There was also presentations but pretty used to them.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
had a level 2 metabolism course – way too easy and had had all the material before
Had a level 1 forensic science course – just for the fun of it
Had a level 3 cancer course – had had some of the material in molecular biology and signal transduction but a lot of new material too. did CRISPR in lab so very interesting

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: pretty much the same. lecturers more down to earth. not a lot of people shows up for lectures because they're all filmed

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: forensic science, Biochemistry: Metabolism, Cancer stem cells and development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Cancer stem cells and development 
forensic science has a lot of readings but the exam is done at home with all notes;)

questions.answer: pretty easy. mostly the slang you have to get accommodated to. and some people's accent

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: met most at my accommodation and during lab at uni

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: very open and happy people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
book trips and not too late because the sem is gonna go by so fast
don't care too much about the uni work

What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting friends from all over the world. having a city somewhere else that I've lived semi-permanently in and know my way around.
